solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boy in the Navy brought into PM’s staff (9)

indicators.note: the boy sits in the Navy's letters
the boy-in-the-Navy group is taken inside the PM's name

blocks.note: Robert Peel, Prime Minister; his name is split open
RN = Royal Navy, split around the boy

explanation.surface: A young sailor is seconded to work in the Prime Minister's office.
explanation.walkthrough: The two containers nest, one inside the other. Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister, a regular crossword PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a firm's personnel are the people it employs.

clue.text: Like some letters offering job with salary? (4-4)

explanation.surface: Someone describes a salaried vacancy and wonders what kind of letters go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'post' as a job, but the definition wants the other post: letters sent with the postage already paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the adjective describes letters whose postage the sender has settled in advance.

clue.text: Meetings with old chums? Being sloshed ruins one (8 )

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that getting drunk spoils a gathering of old friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being sloshed' reads as the reunion's drinking, but it is the instruction to jumble RUINS ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reunions are gatherings of old friends; the question mark admits it is one kind of meeting.

clue.text: That’s a bit unfriendly of Ray perhaps (6)

indicators.note: Ray is one example of a fish

blocks.note: a ray is a flat sea creature; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a class

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a man called Ray is being rather cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name; it is the flat sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish means somewhat aloof or distant, a bit unfriendly.

clue.text: Chat, getting into train at terminus (6)

indicators.note: the answer is found by going inside the following words

explanation.surface: Two people talk as they board a train at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the chat on a train; the answer sits across three of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, informal British: the word means to talk idly and at length.

clue.text: Left road’ll go to one Welsh town (8 )

blocks.note: road = LANE, and the 'll is kept as printed

explanation.surface: Directions: turn left and the road will take you to a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'll of road'll is literal: it supplies the double L after LANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular Welsh town, on the south coast west of Swansea.

clue.text: Despondency at hospital — there’s expression of dissatisfaction (5)

blocks.note: 'the hump' is a fit of low spirits

explanation.surface: A gloomy patient in hospital lets out a disgruntled noise.
explanation.walkthrough: To have the hump is British slang for being fed up or sulky.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is a grunt of doubt or displeasure.

clue.text: Henry, Bill and I stop in front of a Spanish farm (8 )

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Three men halt outside a ranch in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry and Bill look like two friends, but each is an abbreviation: H for the henry and AC for account.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or farm in Spain or Spanish America.

clue.text: Criminal fool, European man disappearing (6)

indicators.note: something disappearing is no longer there, so the word MAN vanishes from the end of GERMAN

blocks.note: a mug is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A foolish crook and a vanishing European man, like a crime report.
explanation.walkthrough: European is GERMAN here, not E; the man that disappears is the tail of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugger is a criminal who robs people in the street.

clue.text: Fall out, apparently, when there’s female around (6)

indicators.note: the female goes around the abbreviation

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird; opened up
APP. is the abbreviation for apparently

explanation.surface: A quarrel seems to break out whenever a woman is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall out' reads as quarrel, but it is the sense 'come to pass'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out can mean to happen, as in 'it fell out that…'.

clue.text: Enjoyment’s returning (apt to pass away) (5,2)

indicators.note: going back, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A gloomy aside: pleasure comes back, but you are likely to die anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Snuff it is British slang for die.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang idiom for dying, from snuffing out a candle flame as a life is put out.

clue.text: Number perform song at uni, getting nervous (7,2)

blocks.note: to sing is to perform a song

explanation.surface: A student is to sing a number at university and feels the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: muscles tighten when someone grows anxious, so the phrase covers the nerves themselves.

clue.text: A new parent, male out to be seen as an alternative (7)

indicators.note: M, for male, is taken out of MOTHER

explanation.surface: A new mother, with the man gone, becomes the other option.
explanation.walkthrough: The parent is MOTHER, whose M is the male that goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more, a different or alternative one.

clue.text: Have great desire to manage a marathon? (4,3)

blocks.note: to long is to desire strongly

explanation.surface: Someone longs to organise a marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'a marathon' is a playful example of a long run, not a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a marathon is one very long race on foot.

clue.text: Indicate site for being redeveloped — it spells an end to trees etc. (15)

definitions.text: it spells an end to trees etc.

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt into a new form

explanation.surface: A planning notice about a site to be redeveloped, warning that the trees will go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being redeveloped' sounds like building work, which fits the loss of trees, but it tells you to rearrange the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertification turns land into desert, ending its trees and other vegetation.

clue.text: Meet liar being devious about computer processing system (8 )

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding route, so the letters wander

explanation.surface: You encounter a dishonest person being shifty about a computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as an anagram signal, but 'being devious' already does that job; 'about' just joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Real-time processing handles data as it arrives, a kind of computer processing system.

clue.text: Extra money? Resent it being squandered (8 )

indicators.note: squandered means scattered, so the letters are dispersed

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that a bonus has been wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks interest as one kind of extra money, the kind earned on savings or charged on loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is money paid on top of a sum lent or saved.

clue.text: One church sure to be freezing cold (8 )

blocks.note: bound = certain, sure (as in 'bound to happen')

explanation.surface: A remark that a church is certain to be bitterly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Anyone who has sat through a winter service in an old English church knows the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebound means held fast by ice, as freezing cold as it gets.

clue.text: Number coming to river, then crossing river, in Scotland? (8 )

indicators.note: THEN goes across the river, holding it inside

explanation.surface: Directions for a river crossing, perhaps somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: Scotland lies in the north of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Scotland is the top part of Britain.

clue.text: Rustic worker by the vegetables (7)

indicators.note: the worker is placed next to the vegetables

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A farm labourer stands beside the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic worker' looks like the definition; only 'Rustic' is, and 'worker' is the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic, as a noun, is a country person, a peasant.

clue.text: Very hot music-making (6)

blocks.note: completes a fixed phrase for scalding food fresh from the oven

explanation.surface: A lively, heated musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Piping on its own means very hot only in the phrase 'piping hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served piping is very hot; piping is also playing a pipe.

clue.text: Indian father is in pain (6)

indicators.note: the father sits inside the pain

blocks.note: an ache is a pain; opened up

explanation.surface: A father from India is suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian looks like someone from India; it is a Native American, the Apache people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, once called American Indians.

clue.text: Supporting ill-mannered person? Hold back! (7)

blocks.note: a bear is a rough, surly person

explanation.surface: Someone is urged not to take the side of a rude person.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'Hold back!' an order, which is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: the verb means to refrain from doing something.

clue.text: Iron Lady? One’s soft on top (6)

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A Thatcher joke: even the Iron Lady has a soft spot on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' was the nickname of Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister, which makes the surface a political joke. The definition describes a soft felt hat worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Country game is on the up in South Africa (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reverses the letters
the reversed word goes inside SA

explanation.surface: A sport is growing in popularity in South Africa, says a report on a country.
explanation.walkthrough: Game is RU, rugby union, which is played in South Africa, so the surface holds together.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the largest country in the world, one of many a solver must choose among.

clue.text: Peter’s lad out getting drunk (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Peter's son is out on the town, getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' reads as a night out, which suits the surface; it is the anagram signal. Plastered is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang synonym for being very heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Vague old bishop’s needing parish priest in tow (7)

indicators.note: the priest is pulled along behind, so comes last

blocks.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: An elderly, woolly bishop needs a parish priest to follow him around.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE is curé, the French parish priest, with its accent dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective describes something unclear or hard to make out.

clue.text: Bird English composer recalled (5)

indicators.note: called back, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A bird brings an English composer to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English composer' wants to be one person, Elgar perhaps; it is E plus Berg, and the whole EBERG turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one kind of diving water bird, known for its courtship dance.

clue.text: Great Dane fouled up place with outdoor cafe (3,6)

indicators.note: messed up, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A big dog makes a mess of a café garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fouled up' fits a dog all too well in the surface; here it only means scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is a garden where tea and refreshments are served outdoors.
